title: French A1: Bonjour, la classe, la famille, et une histoire
topic: French A1 greetings, classroom, family, and everyday life
description: Six gentle lessons for true beginners in French. Learn greetings and introductions, classroom words and colors, family and home, then read and hear a short market story in simple French. Every lesson has a clear explanation, a picture to study, a worked example, and short checks you can do on paper or out loud.
author: Well of Wisdom contributors

lessons.title: Bonjour ! Greetings and politeness
lessons.summary: Say hello, good morning, good evening, and goodbye, and choose salut or bonjour.

content.title: Hello and nice to meet you
content.body:
In French you say **bonjour** (hello, good morning) until the evening, then **bonsoir** (good evening). With friends you can say **salut** (hi or bye, informal). To be polite to an adult you add **monsieur** (sir) or **madame** (maam): **bonjour monsieur**, **bonsoir madame**. **Au revoir** means goodbye. **A bientot** means see you soon. **A plus tard** means see you later.

Politeness matters. You say **merci** (thank you), **merci beaucoup** (thank you very much), **s il vous plait** (please, formal), and **de rien** (you are welcome). When you meet someone you say **enchanté** (nice to meet you, said by a boy or man) or **enchantée** (nice to meet you, said by a girl or woman). The answer is again **enchanté** or **enchantée**, or **de meme** (likewise).

- **bonjour** hello, good morning
- **bonsoir** good evening
- **salut** hi or bye (friends)
- **au revoir** goodbye
- **merci, merci beaucoup** thank you, thank you very much

content.alt: A sunny street in a small French town. Two children face each other and wave. Speech bubbles show bonjour, salut, bonsoir, and au revoir. A shop sign says Boulangerie.
content.caption: Bonjour in the morning, bonsoir in the evening, salut with friends.

content.title: How greetings work
content.problem: Choose the right greeting for the moment and answer politely

steps.text: Look at the time. Before evening, start with bonjour. In the evening, use bonsoir.
Decide the tone. With a friend your age, salut is fine. With an adult you do not know well, use bonjour monsieur or bonjour madame.
Add a polite follow up. After bonjour, say comment ca va (how are you, informal) to a friend, or comment allez vous (how are you, formal) to an adult.
Answer the greeting. Reply bonjour or salut back, then merci if they helped you, and finish with au revoir or a bientot.

content.title: French greetings for beginners
content.note: Watch how native speakers say bonjour, bonsoir, salut, and au revoir. Listen for the nasal on in bon and the silent r at the end of bonjour before you practice the exercises.

content.prompt: Match the French greeting to its English use.
content.explanation: Bonjour covers the day, bonsoir is evening, salut is informal, au revoir closes the talk.
hints: Bonsoir has soir like evening. Salut is short and casual.

content.prompt: Sort each phrase into Formal (vous) or Friendly (tu and salut).

feedback.d1: Monsieur is formal, so this goes to Formal.
feedback.d2: Salut and ca va with tu is friendly.
feedback.d3: Madame is formal, so this goes to Formal.
feedback.d4: Salut and a plus tard is friendly.

content.explanation: Monsieur and madame signal vous and formality. Salut and tu signal friendly speech.
hints: Look for monsieur or madame versus salut.

content.prompt: Put the words in order to say a polite hello to an adult in the morning.
content.explanation: Bonjour monsieur, comment allez-vous is the polite morning greeting to an adult.
hints: Start with Bonjour, then the title monsieur.

lessons.title: Je m appelle... Introducing yourself
lessons.summary: Give your name, ask a name, say how you are, and answer with ca va.

content.title: My name is ... and how are you
content.body:
To give your name say **je m appelle** (I am called) plus your name: **je m appelle Luc**, **je m appelle Amina**. To ask a name with a friend say **comment tu t appelles** (what is your name, friendly). To an adult say **comment vous appelez vous** (what is your name, formal). You can also ask **tu t appelles comment** in speech, same meaning.

To ask how someone is, say **comment ca va** (how is it going, friendly) or **comment allez vous** (how are you, formal). Common answers: **ca va bien** (I am well), **ca va tres bien** (very well), **pas mal** (not bad), **comme ci comme ca** (so so). Ask back with **et toi** (and you, friendly) or **et vous** (and you, formal).

French question intonation rises at the end. You also meet **quel age as tu** (how old are you, friendly) and the answer **j ai dix ans** (I am ten years old, literally I have ten years). For now keep age as listening only.

- **je m appelle ...** my name is ...
- **comment tu t appelles** what is your name (tu)
- **comment ca va** how are you (friendly)

content.alt: Four children in a school courtyard holding name tags. Each tag shows je m appelle plus a first name: Luc, Amina, Jules, Ines. Speech bubbles show comment tu t appelles and enchanté.
content.caption: Je m appelle introduces you. Comment tu t appelles asks a friend in return.

content.title: How to introduce yourself
content.problem: Build a short self introduction and ask back politely

steps.text: Start with a greeting: bonjour for daytime or salut for a friend.
Give your name: je m appelle ... plus your name. Example: je m appelle Luc.
Add a polite close: enchanté or enchantée, matching who is speaking.
Ask back: comment tu t appelles to a peer, comment vous appelez vous to an adult, or simply et toi, comment ca va.

content.prompt: Put the words in order to introduce yourself and ask back to a friend.
content.explanation: Bonjour, je m appelle Ines. Et toi, comment tu t appelles is a complete friendly introduction that asks back.
hints: Start with Bonjour, then je m appelle plus the name.

content.prompt: Choose the best path when you meet a new classmate your age for the first time.

start.text: You see a new classmate at the door. It is morning. What do you do first?

choices.feedback: Good start. Bonjour is right for daytime.
Bonsoir is for evening. It is morning, so bonjour fits better.
A short bonjour helps the other person feel welcome.

askname.text: They answer bonjour. How do you ask their name as a peer?

choices.feedback: Perfect. With a peer you use tu.
Not wrong, but vous is very formal for a classmate your age. Tu is more natural.
Word order is off. The set phrase is comment tu t appelles.

fix_greeting.text: You try again. Which greeting fits a morning meeting with a peer?

choices.feedback: Yes. Bonjour plus je m appelle is a friendly opening.
Bonsoir is for evening. Try bonjour in the morning.

fix_ask.text: Try the question again with the right phrase.

choices.feedback: Yes. That is the friendly form.
Vous is formal. It works with an adult, but with a peer tu is more natural.

good_end.text: They say je m appelle Maya, enchantée. You answer enchanté and you now know each other. You chose the right greeting and the right tu form.

ok_end.text: They answer and you keep talking, but the tone is a bit stiff. Next time try tu with a classmate your age.

content.explanation: With a peer in the morning, bonjour plus comment tu t appelles is the natural path.
hints: Morning is bonjour, not bonsoir. With a peer use tu.

lessons.title: En classe : classroom and colors
lessons.summary: Name classroom objects, say the color, and use un and une correctly.

content.title: Things on the desk
content.body:
In class you see **un stylo** (a pen, masculine), **un cahier** (a notebook, masculine), **un livre** (a book, masculine), **une trousse** (a pencil case, feminine), **une gomme** (an eraser, feminine), **un tableau** (a board, masculine), and **une chaise** (a chair, feminine). **Un** is for masculine nouns, **une** for feminine. You learn the gender with the word.

To say what something is you use **c est** (it is): **c est un stylo bleu** (it is a blue pen), **c est une gomme rose** (it is a pink eraser). Colors: **bleu** (blue), **rouge** (red), **vert** (green), **jaune** (yellow), **noir** (black), **blanc** (white), **rose** (pink). Many color words change a little after a feminine noun: **bleu** becomes **bleue**, **vert** becomes **verte**, but you will hear the pattern before you need to write it perfectly.

Ask **qu est ce que c est** (what is it) and answer **c est un** or **c est une** plus the object. Count to five: **un, deux, trois, quatre, cinq**.

- **c est un stylo** it is a pen
- **c est une trousse** it is a pencil case
- **bleu, rouge, vert, jaune** blue, red, green, yellow

content.alt: A top down view of a school desk with labeled objects: un stylo bleu, un cahier vert, une trousse rouge, une gomme rose, un livre jaune, une chaise. Each label shows un or une.
content.caption: Un for masculine, une for feminine. Learn the word with its un or une.

content.title: How to name what you see
content.problem: Say what an object is and add its color

steps.text: Name the object with c est plus un or une: c est un stylo, c est une trousse.
Pick the color word: bleu, rouge, vert, jaune, rose, noir.
Put the color after the noun: c est un stylo bleu, c est une gomme rose.
Check un versus une by memory: un stylo, une trousse, un cahier, une gomme.

content.prompt: Match the French classroom word to the English.
content.explanation: Stylo is pen, trousse is pencil case, cahier is notebook, gomme is eraser, tableau is board.

content.prompt: Sort each phrase into Masculine (un) or Feminine (une).

feedback.d1: Stylo is masculine, so un stylo, even when blue.
feedback.d2: Trousse is feminine, so une trousse.
feedback.d3: Cahier is masculine, so un cahier.
feedback.d4: Gomme is feminine, so une gomme.
feedback.d5: Livre is masculine, so un livre.
feedback.d6: Chaise is feminine, so une chaise.

content.explanation: Un goes with masculine nouns, une with feminine. Learn them as un stylo, une trousse as a block.
hints: Look at the first word: un or une tells you the bucket.

content.prompt: Put the words in order to say it is a blue pen.
content.explanation: C est un stylo bleu has the order: c est, un, noun, color.
hints: In French the color comes after the object.

lessons.title: Ma famille : family members
lessons.summary: Name parents, siblings, and grandparents, and say mon, ma, mes correctly.

content.title: Who is in your family
content.body:
Family words: **la mere** (mother, also **maman** mom), **le pere** (father, also **papa** dad), **la soeur** (sister), **le frere** (brother), **la grand mere** (grandmother), **le grand pere** (grandfather), **les parents** (parents), **les enfants** (children). You also say **le fils** (son) and **la fille** (daughter).

Possession uses **mon, ma, mes** (my): **mon frere** (my brother), **ma soeur** (my sister), **mes parents** (my parents). **Mon** is with a masculine noun, **ma** with a feminine noun, **mes** with any plural. So **mon pere** but **ma mere**, **mes grands parents** for both. Before a vowel, even a feminine noun takes **mon** for sound: **mon amie** (my friend, feminine).

To introduce your family say **voici ma famille** (here is my family): **voici mon pere, ma mere, et ma soeur**. Ask **tu as des freres et soeurs** (do you have brothers and sisters) and answer **j ai un frere et une soeur** or **je suis enfant unique** (I am an only child).

- **mon pere, ma mere** my father, my mother
- **mon frere, ma soeur** my brother, my sister
- **mes grands parents** my grandparents

content.alt: A simple family tree with photos: grand mere and grand pere at the top, pere and mere in the middle, a brother and a sister at the bottom. Each label shows mon, ma, or mes.
content.caption: Mon for masculine, ma for feminine, mes for plural.

content.title: How to introduce your family
content.problem: Present your family with the right possessive word

steps.text: Start the frame: voici ma famille (here is my family).
Name each person with mon, ma, or mes: mon pere for father, ma mere for mother, mes grands parents for grandparents.
Add a simple detail: elle s appelle Marie, il s appelle Paul, or j ai un frere.
Close politely: ils habitent pres d ici (they live nearby) or on s entend bien (we get along well).

content.prompt: Match the French family word to the English.
content.explanation: La mere is mother, le pere is father, la soeur is sister, le frere is brother, grand mere and grand pere are grandmother and grandfather.
hints: La is often feminine, le is often masculine. Grand means big or old.

content.prompt: Sort each phrase into the correct possessive: mon, ma, or mes.

feedback.d1: Frere is masculine, so mon frere.
feedback.d2: Soeur is feminine, so ma soeur.
feedback.d3: Parents is plural, so mes parents.
feedback.d4: Pere is masculine, so mon pere.
feedback.d5: Grand mere is feminine, so ma grand mere.
feedback.d6: Cousins is plural, so mes cousins.

content.explanation: Mon with masculine singular, ma with feminine singular, mes with any plural.
hints: Check if the noun is masculine, feminine, or plural.

content.prompt: You meet a French exchange student and want to invite their family politely. What is the best path?

start.text: You want to say you would like to meet their family. How do you open?

choices.text: J aimerais rencontrer ta famille si c est possible
choices.feedback: Polite and clear: J aimerais (I would like) softens the request.
Too direct. Famille is not something you give. Use rencontrer (to meet).
Word order is off. You mean rencontrer ta famille.

ask_detail.text: They smile and say avec plaisir (with pleasure). You want to ask if they have siblings. What do you ask?

choices.text: Tu as des freres et soeurs ?
choices.feedback: Yes. That is the natural way to ask.
You want as (have), not es (are). Tu as des freres means you have brothers.

choices.text: Vous avez des freres et soeurs ?
choices.feedback: Correct grammar but very formal for a peer. Tu is warmer here.

fix_start.text: Try again with a polite phrase for meeting someone's family.

choices.feedback: Yes. That is polite and correct.
Je veux is very direct. J aimerais is softer.

fix_ask.text: Try the sibling question again with avoir (to have).

choices.text: Tu as des freres et soeurs ?
choices.feedback: Perfect. Tu as ... is have you ...
Still es instead of as. But they will understand you mean as.

good_end.text: They say j ai une soeur, elle s appelle Lea. You can now say enchanté and ask about Lea. You were polite and used tu correctly.

ok_end.text: They answer politely, but the vous sounds a bit distant for classmates. Next time try tu with a peer.

content.explanation: J aimerais rencontrer ta famille plus tu as des freres et soeurs is polite and peer natural.
hints: Use j aimerais to soften a request. With a peer, use tu and as.

lessons.title: Chez moi et la semaine : home and days
lessons.summary: Name rooms and things at home, and order the days of the week in French.

content.title: At home through the week
content.body:
Home words: **la maison** (house), **l appartement** (apartment), **la cuisine** (kitchen), **le salon** (living room), **la chambre** (bedroom), **la salle de bain** (bathroom), **le jardin** (garden). You say **j habite dans une maison** (I live in a house) or **j habite dans un appartement**.

Days of the week: **lundi** (Monday), **mardi** (Tuesday), **mercredi** (Wednesday), **jeudi** (Thursday), **vendredi** (Friday), **samedi** (Saturday), **dimanche** (Sunday). All days are masculine: **le lundi** means on Monday. You say **aujourd hui c est lundi** (today is Monday) and **demain c est mardi** (tomorrow is Tuesday).

Time words: **le matin** (morning), **l apres midi** (afternoon), **le soir** (evening). A simple plan: **le matin je vais a l ecole, l apres midi je joue dans le jardin**. Numbers to twelve help at home: **six, sept, huit, neuf, dix, onze, douze**.

- **la cuisine, le salon, la chambre** kitchen, living room, bedroom
- **lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche** Monday through Sunday

content.alt: A cutaway view of a small house showing la cuisine with a table, le salon with a sofa, la chambre with a bed, la salle de bain with a sink, and le jardin outside. Labels show lundi through dimanche along the bottom.
content.caption: La maison, four rooms, and the seven days that go with every week at home.

content.title: How to say where and when
content.problem: Say where you live and what day it is

steps.text: Say where you live: j habite dans une maison or j habite dans un appartement.
Name the room: ma chambre est petite, la cuisine est grande.
Give the day: aujourd hui c est lundi, demain c est mardi.
Add a time word: le matin, l apres midi, le soir, plus what you do there.

content.prompt: Put the days of the week in the correct order starting with Monday.
content.explanation: The French week starts with lundi and ends with dimanche, same as ISO order.
hints: Lundi is Monday, the start. Dimanche is Sunday, the end.

content.prompt: Sort each word into the correct room or place at home.

feedback.d1: Le four (oven) is in la cuisine.
feedback.d2: Le lit (bed) is in la chambre.
feedback.d3: Le canape (sofa) is in le salon.
feedback.d4: Le frigo (fridge) is in la cuisine.
feedback.d5: L oreiller (pillow) is in la chambre.
feedback.d6: La tele (TV) is usually in le salon.

content.explanation: Kitchen holds cooking things, bedroom holds sleep things, living room holds rest and TV.
hints: Four and frigo cook and chill, so they are cuisine.

content.prompt: Match the French home phrase to its English.
content.explanation: J habite is I live, salle de bain is bathroom, jardin is garden, aujourd hui c est lundi is today is Monday.
hints: Aujourd hui has hui twice and means today.

lessons.title: Lire et ecouter : Une journee au marche
lessons.summary: Read and hear a short A1 market story, then check what you understood.

content.title: Reading strategy for the story
content.body:
You will read **Une journee au marche** (A day at the market), a short A1 story with the words you already know: greetings, classroom and color words used for fruit, family, and days. Read once without stopping. Circle words you know: **bonjour, merci, maman, papa, rouge, jaune, lundi**. Guess the rest from the picture and the market context.

Listen once if you have the audio or read aloud slowly: French flows in groups, try **bon jour ma man** as one group. Numbers and prices repeat: **un euro, deux euros**. Polite market language is the same as greetings: **bonjour madame, s il vous plait, merci, au revoir**.

After reading you will match phrases, order the story, sort market items by stall, and walk a small choice story at the market. Keep the glosses below the story nearby: they give a quick English nudge without translating the whole page.

content.alt: A colorful French market with three stalls: fruits in rouge and jaune, legumes in vert, and pain and fromage. A mother, a father, a girl and a boy wave and say bonjour. Price tags show 2 euros, 3 euros.
content.caption: Au marche: bonjour, s il vous plait, merci. Colors help you name what you see.

content.title: How to read the story in three passes
content.problem: Read Une journee au marche with confidence even when some words are new

steps.text: First pass: read the title and look at the picture. Predict: who is there, where, and what they want.
Second pass: read the story aloud slowly in groups. Circle bonjour, merci, family words, and colors you know.
Third pass: use the glosses for two or three new words only, then retell the story in one sentence: who went where and what they bought.
Check yourself: answer the three short checks without looking back, then look back to confirm.

content.title: Une journee au marche
content.body:
C est samedi matin. Le soleil brille. Lina et son frere Tom vont au marche avec maman et papa.

Au marche, Lina dit bonjour madame. La marchande dit bonjour, comment ca va. Lina dit ca va bien, merci. Elle voit des pommes rouges, des bananes jaunes, et des tomates vertes.

Papa dit qu est ce que c est. Tom dit c est un melon vert. Maman dit combien ca coute. La marchande dit deux euros. Papa dit s il vous plait, je voudrais un melon et trois pommes.

Apres, ils voient mamie et papi. Lina dit bonjour mamie, bonjour papi. Ils disent enchantés et ils rient. Tom donne une pomme a mamie. Mamie dit merci beaucoup.

Enfin, ils rentrent a la maison. Dans la cuisine, ils mangent le melon. Lina dit c est delicieux. Tout le monde dit merci et a bientot au marche.

content.title: French family story for beginners
content.note: Hear family words like maman, papa, mamie, and papi in a slow A1 story. Listen once without subtitles, then once with French subtitles, and notice bonjour, merci, and the colors you already know.

content.prompt: Put the story moments in the order they happen in Une journee au marche.

items.text: Lina dit bonjour a la marchande.
Papa achete un melon et trois pommes.
Ils voient mamie et papi au marche.
Ils rentrent et mangent le melon dans la cuisine.

content.explanation: First the greeting, then the purchase, then meeting grandparents, then eating at home.
hints: The purchase comes before meeting mamie and papi.

content.prompt: Sort each market item by the stall where Lina saw it.

feedback.d1: Pommes are fruits, even when red.
feedback.d2: Bananes are fruits, even when yellow.
feedback.d3: Tomates are legumes in market language.
feedback.d4: Melon is a fruit, even when its outside is green.

content.explanation: In the story pommes, bananes, and melon are called fruits; tomates are with the vegetables.
hints: In the story only tomates are listed as vert legume color in the vegetable sense.

content.prompt: At the market, how do you buy politely and correctly? Walk the choices.

start.text: You are at the fruit stall. The seller says bonjour. What do you say?

choices.text: Bonjour madame, je voudrais trois pommes s il vous plait
choices.feedback: Polite and clear with madame, je voudrais, and s il vous plait.
Too direct. Add bonjour and s il vous plait and use je voudrais.

choices.text: Je veux trois pommes tout de suite
choices.feedback: Je veux is strong. Je voudrais is softer and more polite at the market.

price.text: She says c est trois euros. You pay. What do you say next?

choices.text: Merci, au revoir et a bientot
choices.feedback: Perfect market close: thanks, goodbye, see you soon.
She already gave the price. Next is thanks and goodbye.
A short merci is expected after you receive the fruit.

fix_start.text: Try again with bonjour and a polite request.

choices.text: Bonjour madame, je voudrais trois pommes s il vous plait
choices.feedback: Yes. That is the polite market phrase.
Salut is friendly but not with madame at the market, and donne is too direct.

fix_price.text: She waits after you paid. What closes the exchange?

choices.feedback: Yes. Merci plus au revoir closes politely.
You left without thanks. They would have liked a merci.

good_end.text: You leave with your apples. The seller smiles and says merci, bonne journee. You used bonjour, je voudrais, s il vous plait, and merci correctly.

ok_end.text: You leave but forgot merci. Next time add merci before au revoir.

content.explanation: At the market you say bonjour madame, je voudrais ... s il vous plait, then merci and au revoir.
hints: Start with bonjour madame, request with je voudrais ... s il vous plait, close with merci.
